3.why: MP P3: 'From the top of the crack, hard 5.10 face climbing (great gear) leads to a ledge'; P4 then starts 'from the belay'. Pitch end is that ledge.
3.text: The belay is on a ledge reached by hard face moves above the top of the crack in the corner.

6.why: MP only says the party 'belayed down near the chimney/gulley' - ambiguous, not stated as the end of P6.

5.why: AAJ: 'On the fifth pitch we traversed right to the base of the summit tower'; pitch 6 then climbs the tower.
5.text: The rightward traverse ends at the foot of the summit tower, where the next pitch starts.

6.why: AAJ: sixth pitch 'took us two-thirds way up the tower (5.10-)'; the other account has the run-out rock leading 'toward cracks and a belay ledge'. Original 'ledge on the run-out face' overstated placement.
6.text: The pitch ends at a belay ledge about two-thirds of the way up the summit tower, after the run-out face.

7.why: Alpinist, seventh pitch: 'traversed up right (5.5) across the upper buttress to a notch on a ridge'; AAJ places the notch between the summit tower and a pinnacle, and the final pitch starts 'from the notch'.
7.text: The belay is in the notch on the ridge between the summit tower and the neighbouring pinnacle.
